column3: “Staggering and stumbling of heart” is rendered “grief or a troubled heart”; NASB adds “both by.”
“One who urinates on a wall” is rendered “one male.”
“I have listened to your voice” is rendered “I have listened to you,” and “I have lifted up your face” as “granted your request.”
“Good on him” is rendered “merry within him,” and NASB adds “for” and “so.”
NASB adds “as” in “became as a stone.”
NASB supplies “a proposal”; the Hebrew says David “sent and spoke with Abigail.”
“Who walked to her foot” is rendered “who attended her.”
